The MNiHEA ingots were prepared by arc-melting a mixture of pure metals (purity ≥ 99.95wt.%), under a Ti-guttered argon atmosphere. All ingots were flipped and remelted for eight times to ensure chemical homogeneity.
Subsequently, the ingots were drop-cast into a water-cooled copper mould to fabricate flats with a dimension of 50×10×5 mm3.
The as-cast flats were homogenized at 1,200 °C for 4 h, and then furnace-quenched (FQ) at a cooling rate of 2 °C/min to ambient temperature.
The homogenized MNiHEA sheets were then gradually cold-rolled at ambient temperature until the thickness reached ∼1.5 mm, without an intermediate stress-relief annealing treatment.
